reversed.description: The Queen of Rings might indicate a focus on material matters to the detriment of emotional or personal care.

upright.tags: Abundance, leadership, stability, prosperity, authority, success, solidity, reliability
upright.description: The King of Rings represents success, financial security, and a commanding presence in the material realm.

reversed.tags: Tyranny, stubbornness, poor financial decisions, mismanagement, rigidity, avarice, risk, imprudence
reversed.description: The King of Rings warns of mismanagement of resources or an overemphasis on material control.

upright.tags: The Water Bearer, The Clouds, The Pot, Numbers 11 and 2, Uranus, Air, Wonder, Travel, "The Star"
upright.description:
The eleventh sign of the zodiac, Aquarius is a fixed air sign ruled by the planet Uranus, and in the body is associated with the circulatory system, calves and ankles. In tarot, Aquarius is related to "The Star", and much like "the Star", it seeks adventure, new experiences, and sacred knowledge with an air of optimism. The water-bearer is a traveler both physically and mentally, exploring new vistas and ideas.

Aquarius, ever the rebel, is struck by wanderlust and regards satiating its own curiosity as a top priority. It concerns itself with passion, progress, and knowledge. This card may also suggest that we need to be aware of our ambitions and attempt to keep ourselves in line with reality.

upright.tags: The Flame, The Head, Number 1, Mars, Fire, The Ram, Vitality, Beginnings, Power, "The Magician"
upright.description:
The first sign of the zodiac, Ares, is a cardinal fire sign. Associated with fortitude and the manifestation of new ideas, Ares brings with it the ability to take on new tasks zealously and with great ambition. In this deck, Ares is most closely associated with "The Magician" tarot card. Ares is ruled by the planet Mars and governs the head, and while it burns bright, it's energy can be temperamental if not honed and aimed carefully. It can be prone to fizzling out before seeing things through to completion - much like a candle. 

Ares symbolizes novelty, creativity, fast-moving projects, drive, and valour. It can also imply shortsightedness, overextending oneself, rash behavior and other fleeting instincts.

upright.tags: The Moon, The Stromach, Water, Number 4, Inuitation, Compassion, "The Moon", "The High Priestess"
upright.description:
The fourth sign of the zodiac, Cancer is a cardinal water sigh and is affiliated with the stomach, chest, womb and the midsection. Cancer is a deeply intuitive card, able to move between two worlds (the water and the earth). However, it is also prone to "wading" through self imposes melancholy. Cancer is associated with "The Moon" and the "The High Priestess", both cards governed by its ruling planet, the moon.

Cancer encourages us to pay attention to our gut instincts, see past the illusions of this world, pay heed to our emotions, and nurture and protect that which we cherish. It can also imply a near-smothering nature, over-sensitivity, and hyper-vigilance.

upright.tags: The Hourglass, The Scroll, Numbers 10 and 1, Saturn, "The Devil", "The World"
upright.description:
The tenth sign of the zodiac, Capricorn is a cardinal earth sign known to rule the skeletal system and joints. Capricorn is also commonly associated with the planet Saturn, and "The Devil" and "The World" in tarot. Much like the skeletal system, Capricorn prides itself on being the foundation of a strong and capable form. Being the tenth sign of the zodiac, Capricorn finds itself towards the end of the astrological cycle. As the sand within the hourglass falls upon Capricorn, it remains undeterred. This card is studious, rigorous, and almost serene.

Capricorn requests we dig our heels in and do the hard work of acknowledging that while we may not have all the time in the world, we must make the most of what time we have.

upright.tags: The Twins, The Arms, The Clouds, Number 3, Mercury, Air, Duality, "The Lovers" , "The Devil"
upright.description:
The third sign of the zodiac, Gemini is a mutable air sign ruled by the planet Mercury. It is associated with communication, duality of thought, and the pursuit of knowledge. Gemini rules the arms, hands, and nervous system. It seeks to reach out, touch, and understand the world on its own merits, through its own experiences and means. Gemini is associated with both "The Lovers" and "The Devil" in tarot - both which feature the same two figures, entwined, whether it through devotion or vice.

Gemini explores dichotomies in thought, curiosity, and the ability to parse extreme highs and lows. It can also be associated with duplicity, deceit, and masking one's true emotions or intentions.

upright.tags: The Sun, The Heart, Number 5, Fire, Pride, Glory, Warpth, "Strength", "The Sun"
upright.description:
The fifth sign of the zodiac, Leo is a fixed fire sign, and this brash, courageous, headstrong lion rules the heart. Leo's dedication to its emotions and ideals can border on zealotry but is a card that sincerely concerned with matters of courage, honour, and pride. In tarot, Leo is associated with "The Sun" and "Strength" (its ruling planet being the sun), and much like the two major arcana cards it radiates optimism and tenacity.

Leo seeks to elevate itself to its highest potential, and reflects our need for recognition and gratitude. It can also suggest being burdened by one's ego and struggling with selfishness., and attempting to make room for others and their perspectives and dreams.

upright.tags: The Clouds, Shoulder Pole, Number 7, Venus, Equality, Indecision, The Scales, "Justice"
upright.description:
The seventh sign in the zodiac, Libra is a cardinal air sigh and governs the lower back, kidneys, and glutes - stabilizing the body. Ruled by the planet Venus, it is often associated with love and attachment, and is affiliated with the tarot card "Justice" - a direct contemporary to the scales of Libra. The carrying pole over the figure's shoulder turns them into a type of scale as they balance the contents, which is apt - Libra is entirely concerned with the nature of balance.

Libra is about resolving conflicts, perusing equality, and seeking reciprocal attachment. However, it can also be associated with indecision, as taking on too many perspectives can leave it incapable of drawing conclusions.

upright.tags: Sun, Moon, Stars, Number 0, Energy, Life, Warmth, Endless Possibility
upright.description:
The only means as by which mirrors reflect images is through the presence of light. The moon reflects the light of the sun as it does not produce any light of its own. The sun operates as our planet's primary source of light, and the warmth  by which all life is made possible. The light of the stars reaches us after thousands of years of travel, further reinforcing The Light's associations with momentum, life-affirming energy, and warmth.

The presence of this card is pervasive throughout the deck, and is intended to facilitate the ability to reflect upon the other cards - simultaneously casting light into out shadows, and making the presence of shadows possible.

upright.tags: Twin Fish, The Sea, The Moon, Numbers 12 and 3, Water, Contemplation, Neptune, "The Moon"
upright.description:
The twelfth and final sign of the zodiac, Pisces is a mutable water sign, associated with the planet Neptune. In tarot, it governs "The Moon" card, and on the human body it rules the feet. Pisces is a culmination of the astrological cycle, and as a result this card is very introspective. The twin fish imply an ability to harmoniously contain multitudes, while also being in perpetual motion with one another. They also exhibit a high sensitivity and deep empathy for all that has come before them. 

Pisces requests we recognize the many lessons in the life cycle, and patiently keep our minds and hearts open too synthesize our dreams and sensitivities. It can also imply pessimism and aimless wandering.

upright.tags: The Bow and Arrow, Flames, Number 9, Fire, Dedication, Novelty, Jupiter, "Temperance"
upright.description:
The ninth sign of the zodiac, Sagittarius is a mutable fire sign and is ruled by the planet Jupiter. On the body, Sagittarius governs the thighs and legs, and that is reflected in the nature of the sign; perpetually moving and propelling itself -forward when it comes to new ideas and ventures. In tarot, it is associated with the "Temperance" card as they are both deeply philosophical and novel, constantly in flux like the liquid that pours back and forth from "Temperance's" cup. Dynamic and ready to strike, Sagittarius pulls back its arrow and narrows its focus.

Sagittarius concerns itself with movement, flow, and dynamism. It also can suggest a need to slow down, reevaluate, and rest.

upright.tags: Scythe, Scorpion's Tail, Lotus, Water, Number 8, Mars, Pluto, Transformation, "Death"
upright.description:
The eighth sign of the zodiac, Scorpio is a fixed water sign and rules the pelvis, hips, and reproductive system. It is governed by the planets Mars and Pluto, and is most closely associated with the "Death" tarot card. While Scorpio and "Death" are both formidable and intimidating at times, this card is truly most concerned with the art of transformation. Scorpio creates, destroys, and reinvents. Like the lotus present on the card, beauty and new growth rises from the mire and mess of life.

Scorpio seeks to take inventory of what is present in its life, what must be retained, and what must be culled. Being a card of transformation, Scorpio sternly acknowledges that we must change.

upright.tags: The Horns, The Throat, Bramble, Number 2, Venus, Earth, The Bull, Loyality, "The Hieorphant"
upright.description:
The second sign of the Zodiac, Taurus is a fixed earth sign. Taurus rules the throat, and is known for strong, steadfast values and an unwavering commitment to its own values. Taurus is a creature of the earth, and therefore grounded to the affairs of the world. Much like its ruling planet, Venus, it pursues love, beauty, and serenity. Much like "The Hieorphant" of tarot, Taurus is a teacher.

Taurus can be interpreted as encouraging individuals to consider their values and dive deep into their structure and significance. It can also be associated with a stubborn commitment to ideals, and an unwillingness to embrace change.

upright.tags: The Maiden, Wheat, Number 6, Earth, Mercury, Logic, Structure, Control, "The Hermit"
upright.description:
The sixth sign of the zodiac, Virgo is a mutable earth sign ruled by Mercury, and it governs the digestive system and abdomen. Much like the tarot card it's closely associated with, "The Hermit", Virgo often seeks solitude in order too engage in deep-seated contemplation and intellectual pursuits. Like the inner workings of the body, Virgo seeks sophisticated structure and logic to operate at its best capacity. This card asks us to take stock of the systems present in our lives, and the phases that must come to pass as time marches on.

Virgo wishes to bring stability and serenity into our lives, but it can come at the expense of cool detachment, or a near impassive approach to what it perceives as inevitable.
